A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original pose-model ablations, motion-generation comparisons, generalization examples, and caption-detail experiments in Table 1 and Figures 4–8.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds original user-preference and motion-stability results in Table 2, plus annotation statistics.

M1.justification: The skeletal conditioning, three rig augmentations, two-stage diffusion training, and long-sequence blending are retained. v2 newly specifies sinusoidal encoding within RestPE and augmentation constraints, but does not establish that these disclosures represent changes to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Truebones Zoo data, five-object novel-dynamics evaluation, and four external rigged objects. The new perceptual assessment and annotation statistics concern existing coverage; Objaverse-XL is proposed only for future work.

E2.justification: The GPT-caption variant, model without rig augmentation, SO-MDMs, and retargeting remain the comparison methods. New Table 2 evaluates this existing set; CharacterMixer and SkinMixer are related-work additions, not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds a distinct perceptual evaluation protocol involving 30 participants comparing rendered videos for realism, prompt alignment, and preference, alongside the Motion Stability Index. These substantially extend evaluation beyond v1's automated assessments, while the original splits and novel-dynamics setup remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds caption-length and noun/verb-distribution analyses in Figures 10–12 and reports visually checking 10K augmented outputs for suitability. Existing component ablations, generalization examples, long-motion demonstrations, and caption-detail analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new participant count concerns evaluation design, while averaged preferences and caption distributions add results without uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds direct perceptual and temporal-stability findings: Table 2 reports 65.60% preference for the proposed method versus 12.40% for the next-highest comparator, without rig augmentation. Its MSI is 8.78 versus retargeting's 9.93 on the displayed scale, although it leads the learned comparators. New annotation plots report mean caption lengths of 12.2, 29.5, and 56.2 words. Original Table 1 values and existing result figures are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10, including the skeletal representations and Appendix C's coverage and novelty definitions, are retained. v2 adds no theorem, proof, substantive derivation, or formal definition for MSI.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and concluding summary retain the same central claims about annotated animal motions, rig augmentation, and generalized motion diffusion. The new evaluations support these claims without introducing a new core contribution.

C2.justification: Section 8 adds substantive limitations concerning omitted root translation, physically implausible augmented rigs, production-use restrictions, and poor zero-shot generalization to humans or open-vocabulary objects. It explains these boundaries and proposes remedies. The new results discussion also distinguishes retargeting's greater smoothness from its limited flexibility for novel prompts.

D1.justification: v2 substantially improves implementation disclosure with GPU and memory requirements, batch sizes of 512/4, training budgets of 400K/1M iterations, and approximate runtimes of 30 hours/4 days. It also specifies 0.8–1.2 bone-length scaling, permitted bone deletions, and RestPE's sinusoidal encoding. These are newly documented details, not established changes to existing training settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds a focused comparison with CharacterMixer and SkinMixer, distinguishing rig blending and retargeting from generative synthesis. Additional citations support sinusoidal encoding, MSI, and future directions involving Objaverse-XL and dynamic mesh synthesis; the overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 renames Conclusion to Discussion and Motion Synthesis to Human Motion Synthesis, adds acknowledgements and an appendix introduction, and updates publication and author information. Most existing prose and the overall section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the preference/MSI table and three annotation-statistics figures. The original dataset table becomes Table 3, and the pose-retrieval and training-coverage figures move and become Figures 13–14. Existing figure images are retained without redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful perceptual and temporal-stability evidence, supplies important training and augmentation details, and states concrete applicability limits absent from v1's concluding discussion. These improve support and transparency. The new user study remains briefly specified, without stimulus/trial details or uncertainty estimates, limiting the strength of the added evidence.
